Regulated MedTech distribution

The first job was building a baseline the business could defend

How a regulated MedTech distributor segmented OTIF, inventory and SKU complexity before corrective action.

48%reported OTIF baseline
2.4xinventory turns
~1,800SKUs in the estate
1,200–1,300targeted SKU range

The situation

A regulated UK MedTech distribution operation presented with a 48% OTIF baseline, 2.4x inventory turns and an SKU estate approaching 1,800 lines. The first question was whether the measure was reliable enough to act on.

The score was real. The question was whether it was locating the cause.

What the measurement journey showed

The 48% baseline understated performance in some customer segments and overstated it in others because lead-time definitions and regulated supply constraints were not represented consistently.

The diagnostic output

OTIF was segmented by customer class, product category and supply-constraint type. Each segment carried an explicit assumption and evidence-quality note, creating a traceable basis for corrective action under ISO 13485.

The decision

The SKU rationalisation target—from approximately 1,800 to 1,200–1,300—was applied only to the segments where excess complexity contributed to service and inventory deterioration. The remaining SKUs were ring-fenced for separate lifecycle review.

Historical operator track record. Company name withheld. Metrics and factual framing follow the confirmed September 2026 case-study source.
